To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a novel acoustic analysis to automatically extract the temporal pattern of DDK and validated it against kinematic measures in individuals with ALS, and that this analysis showed high sensitivity and specificity in differentiating ALS from healthy controls as well as early detection of bulbars declines in individuals with ALS.

an automated acoustic analysis of diadochokineses, which extracts the temporal pattern of speech sound repetitions, showed high sensitivity and specificity in differentiating amyotrophic lateral scleroses (ALS) from healthy controls, and that this analysis outperformed an established clinical measure in detecting early-stage ALS.
we developed an automated acoustic analysis of oral DDK that is capable of detecting bulbar motor involvement early in the disease process in ALS.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of automated acoustic analysis of oral DDK for the early detection of bulbarmotor involvement in ALS.
the development of a new acoustic analysis of DDK that is based on an automatic detection of syllables in the DDK utterances, and the extraction of the temporal pattern of DDK.
the analysis and modeling of human speech.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
an automated acoustic analysis of DDK is a useful and valid tool for assessing the bulbar involvement in ALS, and it is a promising approach for early detection of ALS.
this study provided preliminary validation and evidence that an automated acoustic analysis of oral DDK is useful for early detection of ALS.
the automated acoustic analysis of oral DDK is a valid and sensitive method for detecting bulbar motor involvement early in the disease course of ALS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed an automated acoustic analysis for DDK, which is a promising clinical tool for assessing the bulbar function in ALS.
we have developed an automated analysis to extract temporal patterns of oral diadochkinesi (i.e., syllable repetitions) in ALS.
we have developed a new acoustic analysis for oral DDK that is able to extract a measure, namely cycle-to-cycle variability (cTV), for early detection of ALS.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the acoustic DDK measure, namely, the cTV, has a high diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity for differentiating individuals with bulbar motor decline from healthy controls, and can detect bulbar motor decline in early disease stage.
the acoustic analysis of oral DDK is a promising approach for early detection of ALS.
the cTV measure derived from the acoustic analysis of the oral DDK task has the potential to serve as a novel bulbomotor assessment in early-stage ALS.
